title: Finite normal models over reduced purely inseparable base changes
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $K/k$ a finite purely inseparable extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], and $W$ a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $X=W_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] and assume $X$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $f:N\to X$ be a finite surjective morphism with $N$ integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense open subscheme such that $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism. Put $Y=N\times_k K$ and $Z=(W\times_k K)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-pc-base-change, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Assume every local ring of $Y$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then $Y$ and $Z$ are integral, $Y$ is normal, and the morphism $Y\to W\times_k K$ induced by $f$ has a unique factorization $p:Y\to Z$ through the reduction immersion, with $p$ finite and surjective. The projection to $W$ induces $q:Z\to X$; its underlying map is a homeomorphism. The open $V=q^{-1}(U)$ is dense, $p^{-1}(V)$ is dense in $Y$, and $p^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an isomorphism. In addition the canonical closed immersion $X\times_k K\to W\times_k K$ identifies $(X\times_k K)_{\mathrm{red}}$ with $Z$, and the open $U\times_k K$ of $X\times_k K$ is reduced and canonically isomorphic to $V$ over $W\times_k K$.

source.place: Tag 0C3N (varieties-lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields), finite-model part of the affine reduced field-change comparison; specialization with a supplied finite model whose field base change is normal.

proof.text: Write $W_K=W\times_kK$ and $X_K=X\times_kK$. By [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep], the projections $Y\to N$ and $W_K\to W$ are homeomorphisms. The reduction immersions $X\to W$ and $Z\to W_K$ are homeomorphisms and $Z$ is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism]. Thus $Y$ has the nonempty irreducible underlying space of $N$, and $Z$ has that of $X$. Every local ring of $Y$ is a domain by hypothesis, hence has no nonzero nilpotent; $Y$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The reduced irreducible characterization in [def-pc-integral-scheme] now makes both $Y$ and $Z$ integral. The asserted normality of $Y$ is precisely its assumed local-ring condition.

source.place: Tags 01J0 (schemes-definition-reduced), 01J4 (schemes-definition-reduced-induced-scheme); Properties Tag 01ON; purely inseparable homeomorphism as in Morphisms 04DF

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] to the reduced source $Y$ and its map to $W_K$, giving $p:Y\to Z$. Apply it also to the reduced source $Z$ and the projection $Z\to W$, giving $q:Z\to X$. These factorizations are unique: a closed immersion is a homeomorphism onto its image with a surjective map of structure sheaves [def-weil-closed-immersion], so both the underlying map and the sheaf map of a factorization are determined by their composite. On spaces the defining equation $i_Xq=\operatorname{pr}_W i_Z$ expresses $q$ as the composite of the homeomorphisms in step 1 and the inverse of $i_X$. Hence $q$ is a homeomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0356 (schemes-lemma-map-into-reduction); uniqueness from the definition of closed immersion

proof.text: Let $a:X_K\to W_K$ be the base change of $i_X$. It is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] and is a homeomorphism by the universal-homeomorphism assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism] applied to $W_K\to W$. Put $T=(X_K)_{\mathrm{red}}$ with immersion $j:T\to X_K$. Both $T$ and $Z$ are reduced. The factorization lemma [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] gives $b:Z\to X_K$ with $ab=i_Z$ (the image of $a$ is all of $W_K$), then $c:Z\to T$ with $jc=b$, and $d:T\to Z$ with $i_Zd=aj$. Now $i_Zdc=ajc=ab=i_Z$, so $dc=1$. Also $ajcd=i_Zd=aj$, so first cancel $a$ and then $j$ to get $cd=1$; cancellation is the uniqueness argument of step 2. Thus $d$ is the required canonical identification of $T$ with $Z$ over $W_K$.

source.place: Tag 0356 (schemes-lemma-map-into-reduction), applied successively; Morphisms Tags 01QR and 054M

proof.text: Let $h=f_K:Y\to X_K$. By [def-pc-base-change] this is the pullback of $f$ along $X_K\to X$. Consequently $h$ is finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange] and surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. With $c,d$ from step 3, put $\widetilde p=cp:Y\to T$. The equations $aj\widetilde p=abp=i_Zp=ah$ give $j\widetilde p=h$ by cancellation of the closed immersion $a$. Moreover $d\widetilde p=dcp=p$ since $dc=1_Z$. These are equations of scheme morphisms, identifying the lift and its composite with $p$.

The square with sides $\widetilde p:Y\to T$, $h:Y\to X_K$, $j:T\to X_K$, and $1_Y$ is cartesian. To verify the universal property, let $S$ be any scheme with maps $u:S\to Y$ and $v:S\to T$ satisfying $hu=jv$. Then $j\widetilde p u=hu=jv$, hence $\widetilde p u=v$ by cancellation of the closed immersion $j$ as proved in step 2. Thus $u$ itself is the unique map to the upper-left $Y$ with the required composites. It follows that $\widetilde p$ is the base change of the finite morphism $h$ along $j$, and is finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]. It is surjective because $h=j\widetilde p$ is surjective and $j$ is bijective on points. The isomorphism $d:T\simeq Z$ then gives the same properties for $p=d\widetilde p$.

source.place: Tag 01WL (morphisms-lemma-base-change-finite); elementary fibre-product universal property using cancellation of the reduction closed immersion

proof.text: The given isomorphism $f^{-1}(U)\simeq U$ base changes to an isomorphism $h^{-1}(U_K)\simeq U_K$, where $U_K=U\times_kK\subseteq X_K$ [def-pc-base-change]. To see this directly, base change its inverse as well; their composites remain identities. The left side is an open of the reduced $Y$, so its stalks, and hence the stalks of $U_K$, are reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. In the identification $T\simeq Z$, the inverse image of $U_K$ is $V=q^{-1}(U)$: composing either map to $X$ with $i_X$ gives the projection to $W$, so they agree by uniqueness in step 2. On each affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $U_K$, the restriction of $j$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/\sqrt{0})\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]; since $U_K$ is reduced, $\sqrt{0}=0$. It follows that $V\simeq U_K$ canonically over $W_K$. Moreover $p^{-1}(V)=h^{-1}(U_K)$, and $p$ on this open is the preceding isomorphism followed by the inverse of $V\simeq U_K$.

source.place: Tags 01J0 and 01J4 (schemes-definition-reduced, schemes-definition-reduced-induced-scheme); base change of a specified isomorphism and restriction of the nilradical quotient

proof.text: The homeomorphism $q$ carries $V$ to the dense open $U$, so $V$ is dense. Also $U$ is nonempty because $X$ is nonempty and $U$ is dense. Surjectivity of $f$ makes $f^{-1}(U)$ nonempty. It is open in the irreducible space $N$, hence dense (any two nonempty opens in an irreducible space meet). The homeomorphism $Y\to N$ of step 1 carries $p^{-1}(V)=h^{-1}(U_K)$ to $f^{-1}(U)$, so $p^{-1}(V)$ is dense in $Y$. This proves both density assertions.
